title: The Little Otter Who Found His Friend Again
titleZh: 重新找回朋友的小水獭

illustrations.alt: Otto the little otter brags on a floating log in the river while Cara the crane stands sadly on the riverbank with her head down, quarrel mood, watercolor style
Otto the little otter sits alone on the riverbank under the starry night sky, hugging his tail, looking up at Cara the crane's nest in a distant tree, lonely mood, watercolor style
Otto the otter and Cara the crane sit side by side on the floating log, splashing water happily, laughing together, golden sunset over the river, warm friendship mood, watercolor style

summary: Otto the otter and Cara the crane are the best of friends — until one silly quarrel makes Otto say something mean and Cara fly away. At first Otto tells himself he doesn't care. But playing alone isn't any fun at all. Can he swallow his pride, say sorry, and find his friend again?
moral: True friendship means caring more about each other than being right. A friend who says sorry and means it is worth far more than winning an argument.
moralZh: 真正的友谊，是把对方放在心上，比“谁对谁错”更重要。一个真心说“对不起”的朋友，比赢了一场争吵珍贵得多。

vocabulary.meaning: 吞下；咽下（这里指咽下骄傲）

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: By the sparkling Silver River, there lived a little otter named Otto. He could slide down muddy banks, dive deeper than anyone, and float on his back without a single splash. And his very best friend in the whole wide world was Cara the crane.

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Every morning, Cara would call down from the sky, and Otto would splash up out of the water. Together they would play hide-and-seek in the reeds, race to the far bend of the river, and invent new games that only the two of them knew how to play.

paragraphs.speaker: Cara
paragraphs.text: "Otto! Otto! Look at the big log floating down the river! First one to ride it wins — ready, set... GO!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Otto splashed and swam with all his might. He reached the big log first and scrambled on top, dripping and proud. Cara fluttered down beside him a moment later, laughing.

paragraphs.speaker: Cara
paragraphs.text: "You win! You're so fast in the water, Otto. Nobody can beat you!" (she giggles)

paragraphs.speaker: Otto
paragraphs.text: "I know! I win EVERY time. Water games are my thing. You're only good at flying, Cara. You can't even dive!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Cara's smile disappeared. She didn't say anything for a long moment. Then her wings drooped, and she turned her head away.

paragraphs.speaker: Cara
paragraphs.text: "That wasn't a nice thing to say, Otto. I like flying games too, you know. And I try to be happy for you when you win."

paragraphs.speaker: Otto
paragraphs.text: (crossing his little arms) "Well, I'm still the winner. Winners don't have to be nice."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Cara's eyes filled with tears. Without another word, she spread her wings and flew high into the sky — away, away, away, until she was just a tiny dot above the hills. Otto watched her go. He tried to feel proud, but his tummy felt funny and tight.

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: The next morning, Otto slid down the bank and looked up at the sky. No Cara. He swam to the far bend of the river. No Cara. He called out her name, but only the echo answered.

paragraphs.speaker: Otto
paragraphs.text: "Hmph. Who needs her? I can play by myself. I don't need ANYONE."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: But playing alone was boring. Splashing alone was lonely. And floating on his back with nobody to race him... that was the loneliest of all. Otto tried to tell himself he didn't care, but his heart knew better.

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: That night, a wise old frog named Fern hopped up beside Otto. She looked at his long, sad face and croaked softly.

paragraphs.speaker: Fern
paragraphs.text: "Hello, little otter. I've never seen a lonelier smile. What happened to your friend with the white wings?"

paragraphs.speaker: Otto
paragraphs.text: "She flew away because I... because I said she can't dive. And I told her winners don't have to be nice. But it was TRUE! I AM a winner!" (his voice wobbles)

paragraphs.speaker: Fern
paragraphs.text: "Hmm. Being right and being kind are two different things, little otter. You were right that you won. But you were wrong to make your friend feel small. Which do you think matters more — being right, or having your best friend back?"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Otto stared at the moonlit river. He remembered Cara's drooping wings and the tears in her eyes. And suddenly, winning felt very small and very cold. --- --- ---

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: At sunrise, Otto swam all the way to the big willow tree where Cara had built her nest. He climbed the lowest branch and called up as gently as he could.

paragraphs.speaker: Otto
paragraphs.text: "Cara? It's me, Otto. I'm... I'm sorry. Really, truly sorry. I was proud and stubborn and mean. Winning meant nothing without you there to share it."

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: There was a long silence. Then a white head peeked over the edge of the nest, and two bright eyes looked down at him.

paragraphs.speaker: Cara
paragraphs.text: "You said winners don't have to be nice, Otto." (a small pause) "But you know what? The nicest thing anyone ever said to me was that I'm your best friend. And I'd like to hear it again — if you mean it."

paragraphs.speaker: Otto
paragraphs.text: "I mean it! You're my best friend, Cara. I promise. And from now on, being kind matters more to me than winning. Cross my heart!"

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: Cara flew down and landed right beside him on the branch. She nuzzled his wet head, and they both laughed so hard that a few sleepy leaves fell off the tree.

paragraphs.speaker: Cara
paragraphs.text: "Race you to the floating log? This time, let's ride it together. Both winners, side by side."

paragraphs.speaker: Otto
paragraphs.text: "Deal! But only if you teach me your flying game after. Even if I'm terrible at it!" (he grins)

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: And so, Otto and Cara sat side by side on the floating log, drifting down the Silver River under the golden sun. Otto learned Cara's flying game (he was very bad at it), and Cara learned to dive (she was even worse). But they laughed the whole way — because friends don't need to be the best at everything. They just need to be there for each other.

paragraphs.speaker: Narrator
paragraphs.text: From that day on, Otto never said "I'm the winner, so I don't have to be nice" again. Instead, he learned the best winning of all: saying sorry when you're wrong, forgiving when you're hurt, and keeping your best friend close. Good night, little dreamers. Remember — being kind is always a win.
